relationships.subject: erenumab
relationships.evidence_quote: The fully human monoclonal antibody erenumab, which targets the calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) receptor, was licensed in Switzerland in July 2018 for the prophylactic treatment of migraine.

relationships.subject: erenumab
relationships.evidence_quote: The overall reduction in MMD was 7.6 ± 7.0 compared to baseline (p < 0.001).

relationships.subject: erenumab
relationships.evidence_quote: The most reported AE was constipation in 21.2%, followed by insufficient effect in 6.1%, lack of efficacy in 6.1%, diarrhea in 5.1% and injection site reaction in 2.0% of the study population.

key_findings: In 172 Swiss patients, 6 months of erenumab reduced HIT-6, monthly migraine days (7.6) and acute medication days, and reduced migraine impact on partners and children (IMPAC).
Constipation was the most frequent adverse event (21.2% of AEs); no SAE was treatment-related.
